Leaving a ground rice-and-dal batter at warm room temperature so wild lactic-acid bacteria and yeast raise it and sour it.
content.how_to: Mix the ground rice and dal with salt, cover loosely, keep somewhere warm (around 25-30 C) for 8-16 hours until the batter has roughly doubled and smells pleasantly sour with visible bubbles.
content.sensory_cues: Volume more than doubled; domed, bubbly surface; clean sour smell.
content.failure_modes: Too cold or too short: flat batter, no rise, dense idli. Too long or too warm: over-sour, thin batter.

Heating a thin liquid dish only until it foams up at the edges, then taking it off - never letting it roll to a hard boil, which would turn it bitter and cloudy.
content.how_to: Keep the heat low to medium; watch for a white froth rising up the sides and the surface just trembling, then switch off. For rasam this is the moment the raw smell of the tamarind and spice powder disappears.
content.sensory_cues: A ring of froth climbs the pan; the liquid is aromatic, not raw-smelling; no violent bubbling.
content.failure_modes: Hard boiling: bitter, muddy, the fresh aroma is cooked off.

Ladling a thin fermented batter onto a hot, lightly greased flat griddle and spreading it outward in a spiral with the base of the ladle, so it sets into a large thin pancake or a crisp crepe.
content.how_to: Heat a tava until a drop of water skitters and evaporates. Wipe with a little oil or ghee. Pour a ladle of batter at the centre and, with the ladle base, spread it outward in a widening spiral. Drizzle oil at the edges; cook until the underside is golden and lifts freely, then fold or roll.
content.sensory_cues: The edges lift and turn lacy-brown; the surface loses its wet sheen; the dosa slides when nudged.
content.failure_modes: Griddle too cool: batter sticks and tears when spread. Griddle too hot or too dry: batter seizes before it can be spread thin.

content.how_to: Drain the soaked ingredient, grind in short bursts adding cold water a splash at a time, until the paste is smooth and light; grind urad dal fine and fluffy, rice a little coarse.
content.sensory_cues: Urad paste is white, smooth and holds a soft peak; a drop floats in water.
content.failure_modes: Too much water or over-grinding rice: thin batter, flat idli.
